title: Customer signal microtome and futures playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft: a small, surgical approach to turn messy customer voice into implementable micro-probes. I call the pattern the 'microtome' — slice customer signals very thin so we can test low-effort fixes and measure impact quickly.

Context / why now:
- Last two weeks of field interviews and support triage produced many overlapping asks around latency spikes, unexpected token costs, and model fallback behavior. No single epic captures the breadth; we need many tiny experiments.
- Product + Eng asked for a compact set of candidate probes that are low-cost to implement and high-value to validate.

High level goals (success metrics):
- Reduce top-3 customer-reported latency incidents by 30% for affected routes (measured by Console route dashboard) within 6 weeks for any probe rolled to customers.
- Validate at least 3 distinct cause→remedy mappings (e.g., small-context batching misconfig → routing tweak) with data.
- Produce 2 'ship or kill' decisions for product features (one should be a quick UX/Docs fix).

Voice slices (thin, representative customer quotes):
1) "We see token cost jump when the conversation branches — can't predict bills" — enterprise search app (large doc indexing)
2) "Fallback to smaller model sometimes returns hallucinated tool calls" — fintech customer
3) "When traffic surges our dedicated pool gives up and the app stalls for minutes" — mid-market SaaS

Surgical probes (hypothesis -> quick experiment -> signal to watch -> owner):
A. Probe: 'prefix-aware batching tweak'
   Hypothesis: Many latency spikes come from batching mixing long prefixes with short queries; routing by prefix-length reduces queueing and average tail latency.
   Experiment: Add a routing rule for the busiest route to split requests into two queues (short < 128 tokens, long >= 128) for one week. No model change.
   Signal: 95th percentile latency per route, queue depth, CPU/GPU utilization.
   Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Ethan L.)
   Estimated effort: 2 sprint-days (config + runbook)

B. Probe: 'KV-cache priority warming for chat resumes'
   Hypothesis: Repeated conversation resumes miss cache warming, causing repeated decode rounds and cost. Pre-warm KV cache on common conversation resumption patterns.
   Experiment: Instrument two customer routes, enable proactive KV fetch for top-5 resumed prefixes for 3 days.
   Signal: per-token throughput, tokens/sec, customer reported latency, cost delta.
   Owner: applied-ml (Marta V.)
   Effort: 3 sprint-days + lightweight feature flag

C. Probe: 'graceful fallback policy tuning (safety-first)'
   Hypothesis: When capacity constrained, fallback to certain model variants causes hallucination regressions. A safety-first fallback (prioritize model with safety tuning) reduces hallucination incidents at cost of modest latency.
   Experiment: Route 10% of traffic to safety-first fallback for 72 hours. Collect hallucination rate from eval set + customer QA.
   Signal: hallucination incidence, error reports, latency uplift.
   Owner: product-hosted-api (Jonah G.)
   Effort: 1 week including eval harness

D. Probe: 'route-level cost quickwins (doc-level dedupe)'
   Hypothesis: Several customers pay duplicated embedding costs because identical doc batches run multiple times. Small dedupe in ingest reduces embedding units used and tokens billed.
   Experiment: Add a dedupe layer to one customer's ingest pipeline for 2 weeks and report embedding units used.
   Signal: embedding units/month, customer bill variance, query latency.
   Owner: solutions-engineering (Priya M.)
   Effort: 3–4 days (script + rollback plan)

Prioritization rubric (microtome rules):
- Speed: can we deliver a measurable experiment in <= 2 weeks? Priority++
- Reversibility: low blast radius or feature-flagged -> Priority++
- Signal clarity: single metric that shows directionality -> Priority++
- Cross-impact: if it helps multiple customers (e.g., batching) -> Priority++

Quick wins (low-effort, high-probability):
- Docs blurb + sample config for customers about "designing conversation prefixes to avoid token spikes" (owner: developer-experience; 1 day)
- Template runbook for SRE on "temporary route split" to quickly isolate noisy routes (owner: SRE; 1–2 days)

Open questions / unknowns:
- How many routes share the same prefix-length distribution? Need quick query histogram from Console (ask observability).
- Are customers who report token cost spikes using batching incorrectly (client-side)? Add a short customer survey in CS touch.
- Safety-first fallback: do we have an automated eval to detect hallucination regressions in near-real-time, or do we need manual QA?

Data requests (small & actionable):
- Observability: 7-day histogram of token-length per incoming request for top 10 noisy routes (owner: observability team)
- Billing: per-route embedding units by client id for last 30 days (owner: finance analytics)
- Customers: 5-minute post-incident interviews for two high-impact customers to trace playbook (owner: CS low-touch ops)

Next steps / immediate plan (1–2 week horizon):
1) Mobilize micro-probe A and B in parallel behind feature flags. Kick off Monday.
2) Run quick customer-scorer (5 customers) to pick candidate route for dedupe probe D.
3) Draft a short release note and FAQ for any customer-facing KB entries.
4) Daily 15-minute sync for probe owners (Mon–Fri) to keep experiments tight.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Experiments may cause transient SLA blips. Mitigation: limit to <10% traffic, auto-rollback triggers on error budget thresholds.
- Risk: Signal noise (can't detect small improvements). Mitigation: predefine effect size we consider meaningful and power calculation for metric windows.

Appendix (cheap artifacts to ship with probes):
- Quick-run measurement notebook (observability query + charts)
- Customer-facing one-pager for each probe with roll-forward/rollback checklist
- A short survey template to collect follow-up qualitative feedback

Notes to self:
- Use the 'microtome' name in PR titles so we can track related artifacts: e.g., "microtome/kv-warm-flag"
- Keep all experiments behind a single Canary org id for easier billing and impact measurement

End of draft.

Unresolved: pick one customer route for dedupe probe by Friday (2025-06-20).
summary: Working draft that breaks down customer feedback into small, testable probes (microtome metaphor). Probes target batching, kv-cache warming, fallback policies, and embedding dedupe. Intended owners and immediate next steps included.
